ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a square, with 8 semicircles arranged inside along the four sides; on each side there are two semicircles, and their diameters each occupy half of that side. The figure is symmetric about the horizontal midline and vertical midline of the square, and there is a circle in the center, tangent to these surrounding semicircles. Reasoning: The side length of the square is 2. From the figure it can be seen that each side is divided into two equal semicircle diameters, so the diameter of each semicircle is 1, and the radius is 1/2. Establish a coordinate system, making the square [0,2] × [0,2]. Since the figure is horizontally and vertically symmetric, the center of the desired circle is at the center of the square, namely (1,1). Take the semicircle on the left side of the upper side; the center of its complete circle is the midpoint of its diameter (1/2,2), and the radius is 1/2. The distance between the two circle centers is sqrt((1-1/2)^2 + (1-2)^2) = sqrt(1/4+1) = sqrt(5)/2. The two circles are externally tangent, therefore this distance is equal to r + 1/2, so r = sqrt(5)/2 - 1/2 = (sqrt(5)-1)/2.
